Subject: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike — reserved throughput exhausted

Marissa,

We started seeing a high-severity degradation at 07:45 PDT in our PB-prod environment that looks like a reserved-capacity shortfall on your side. Key metrics: 95p response latency jumped from ~1.1s to ~3.8s, average tail latency at 99p up to 6s, and 5xx error rate increased from ~0.3% to 6.4% across our live routes. Our dashboard shows the dedicated GPU pool "pb-prod-1" at 100% reserved throughput consumption and sustained queueing (tokens queued).

This is impacting authorizations and causing user-visible failures for ~12% of requests. We need immediate remediation and an ETA for recovery. Please advise: can you surface an ops/eng bridge now and what mitigations do you plan to apply? We are also prepared to pause non-critical analytics traffic if that helps.

We require executive visibility if this cannot be stabilized in the next 60 minutes.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, PriorityBank

Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike — technical triage notes

Quick technical readout (on-call):

Observations:
- The dedicated pool pb-prod-1 is exhibiting sustained GPU util near 98% and KV cache pressure (cache miss ratio up ~4x) starting ~07:40 PT.
- Token distribution shows a large spike from a single API client key (PriorityBank analytics-batch) generating long sequences; that client accounts for ~60% of token throughput in the 07:30–08:00 window.
- No memory OOMs recorded, so saturation is throughput/KV-cache/warms-related rather than a model crash.

Immediate mitigations we can execute now (est. 5–15m to take effect):
1) Apply a 50% token-rate throttle to the analytics-batch key for 2 hours — should free headroom quickly.
2) Hot-swap routes for interactive production on pb-prod-1 to the quantized-v1 variant (memory-friendly) — short-term quality delta expected, recovery 10–15m.
3) If throttling + quantized fallback does not restore tail latency within 20m, request a 2-node burst allocation (adds ~40% capacity) — needs authorization to consume burst spend.
4) Put automated preemption policy for non-priority customers on this pool (ops policy change) — requires config window but can be applied in next 2–4 hours for stability.

Estimated impact: throttling + quantized fallback should reduce 95p latency by ~40–60% and bring 5xx back toward baseline within the 20–30m window.

I’ll create a short ops ticket with the throttle key and rollout commands and hold on the change until Marissa confirms with Priya.

—Priyom (on-call infra)
